mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, reducing corporate investments and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day S&P returns are positive more than 40% of the time when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment rate signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If S&P returns are negative more than 30% when UNRATE drops sharply, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP and low federal funds rates indicate economic growth with easy monetary policy, boosting S&P 500 over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the joint effect doesn't correlate positively, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth in late-cycle indicates inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If S&P returns are positive when INDPRO grows, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth signals a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If S&P returns are negative more than 60% of the time with employment growth, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P returns are negative when housing starts exceed 1.2 million, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment and high federal funds rates signal tightening, leading to negative S&P returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the joint effect doesn't correlate negatively, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales growth in early recovery signals economic rebound, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P returns are negative when retail sales grow, the hypothesis is invalid.
